findings.anchor: docs/plans/the-crew-surface-is-one-tool-and-a-few-verbs.html:24 (s6 depends-on; s6 write paths line 186, s5 write paths lines 163-165)
findings.reason: the plan's own earlier wiring finding was this same shape (§4 writing a path §2 owns with no edge) and was repaired by adding a dependency, so this collision needs the same edge (s6 depends-on s5, or the followup sequencing §5 after §6).
findings.text: §5 and §6 both declare `reckon/mcp.py`, and both edit the shared `_crew` function (§5 adds eight actions to it; §6 moves its inline view dispatch out to `mcp_views.py`), yet the declared graph orders neither before the other — a roadmap releasing §5 and §6 concurrently launches two exclusive-scope writers at the same region of one file and one change is lost or reworked

findings.reason: the node implementing §7 as written cannot pass its own gate, so the measure must be restated as a net (base minus the folded names plus the new parents) or the gate is quietly reworded until it passes and measures nothing.
findings.text: the §7 measure reads "the visible leaf count ... is at most the base count minus the folded names", but the node folds eleven names away (repair-status, repair-review, budget-lift, budget-lifts, budget-reset, preflight, check-manifest, check-review, resume-ready, redispatch, unwatch) and introduces three new leaves `crew repair`, `crew budget`, `crew check` that do not exist in the command tree today (verified: no `@crew.command(name="repair"|"budget"|"check")` anywhere under reckon/), so a correct implementation leaves base−11+3 = base−8 and the assertion demanding ≤ base−11 fails

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — resolved each cited symbol: `land_merge` (reckon/crew/merge.py:309), `_release_after_promotion` (reckon/crew/promotion_release.py:476), `narrow_claim` (reckon/crew/claims.py:90) and `release_claim` (:128); `reckon/mcp_views.py` exists and `_crew` (reckon/mcp.py:1621) dispatches its views inline as §6 states; `crew list` builds its own rows (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:211); the extensionless hrefs resolve as `<path>.html` — docs/research/what-coordinators-report-about-the-reckon-surface.html carries `s3`/`s4`, docs/plans/every-plan-write-goes-through-edit-plan.html carries `s3`, and docs/plans/consumers-read-reckon-through-verbs.html exists.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — every implementable section names a measurable done-when with a declared negative control, including §3 (three guards, plus a control that truncates the dry run to its first failure), §4 (marker check refuses a dropped change), §6 (parity control registers a view on the MCP tool only) and §7 (control alters one successor's answer).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — evidence and gate measurements land in the run's report/evidence, and the only temporary trees named (the §3 and §4 test repositories) are test scaffolding, not the evidence store.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new paths and symbols carry no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags (`tombstones.py`, `mcp_views.py`, `test_crew_families_fold.py`, `crew check --manifest`), and no comment encodes changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7's mechanism does not produce its own done-when: it folds eleven names away but also adds three leaves that do not exist today, so the visible count lands at base−8, not `base − (folded names)` as the measure demands.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each node names one deliverable closed by one gate; §3's three changes all attach to `crew complete`'s refusal surface and are measured by one test file.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §5 and §6 both declare `reckon/mcp.py` in their write paths with no ordering edge between them (§5 depends on s4 and `every-plan-write-goes-through-edit-plan#s3`; §6 depends on s2 and s4).
